answer.rationale: Finance's 18% cut is hard and the low-cost vendor's quote alone meets it.  Memory c2 (the prior switch) reports accurate invoicing and quick onboarding, which addresses the main cost-of-ownership concern; verifying it guards against switching on a stale or rosy record.  The assembly line's zero buffer (94% of committed volume) means any delivery interruption is severe, so the first shipment will be a guarded test batch, not a full volume migration.  If the archive check confirms the record, we switch primary and accept the 14-day countdown; if it reveals discrepancies in the low-cost vendor's performance history, we fall back to renegotiate_terms with the incumbent, accepting a smaller cost saving to protect the delivery line.  memory_c5's defer option is ruled out because the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, and deferring would strand the line.
